meta.title: App Audio Router — Send one app's audio to several devices at once
meta.description: Free, open-source per-app audio routing for Windows 10 / 11: one application → many playback devices, with per-device delay compensation and volume balance. No virtual audio driver required.

hero.title: One program's sound, headed for many devices at once
hero.tagline: Per-app audio routing for Windows: send one program's sound to several playback devices at once, each with its own delay compensation and its own volume.
hero.description: Free and open source. The whole app is a single native binary calling the Windows Core Audio API directly — there is no virtual audio driver to install and no helper executable. Routing applies to running programs immediately, no restart needed.
hero.note: MSI / NSIS installer · Free, no ads · English / 简体中文 interface

illustration.label: UI sketch: the process sits in the centre, playback devices on the outer ring

features.title: Route, align, balance
features.description: No mixer graph, no virtual cable: pick a program, pick devices, click once. Every capability comes from the Windows Core Audio API — nothing is installed into the audio stack.

routing.title: One app → many devices
routing.description: Select one or more processes and one or more playback devices; the audio is mirrored to all of them live. A running program never needs a restart, and stopping sends it back to the system default.

delay.title: Per-device delay compensation
delay.description: A signed millisecond value per device: positive holds a fast device back, negative marks the earliest one. Wired speakers and a Bluetooth headset sound at the same moment, with configurable range and step.

volume.title: Per-device volume balance
volume.description: A 0–100 % value per device, attenuating it relative to the loudest one in the route. Changes are pushed to running routes and are audible immediately.

native.title: No driver · no dependencies
native.description: Routing, duplication, delay and gain are all done by the app itself — no virtual audio driver, no third-party executable, and nothing left behind on uninstall.

memory.title: Auto-remember · tray resident
memory.description: Routing rules are stored per executable name and restored when the program plays again. The tray icon keeps it out of the way, with optional close-to-tray and start-with-Windows; device and process lists follow the audio engine on their own.

scenarios.title: The moments it was built for
scenarios.description: Every scenario below is a combination of the real capabilities above — nothing invented.

screenshotAlt.dark: The same multi-device audio route displayed in the dark theme

sibling.title: Keep your headphones on, let others hear too
sibling.description: The headset is yours, the speakers are for everyone else: route the player to both at once, and nobody has to take the headphones off or crowd around.

sync.title: The Bluetooth headset no longer lags
sync.description: Bluetooth codecs add inherent latency, so wired speakers and a headset never line up on their own. Give the fast path a millisecond delay and both devices sound at the same moment.

balance.title: Headset too quiet, speakers too loud
balance.description: A percentage volume per device, attenuated relative to the loudest one. The first device is driven natively by Windows; every mirrored path is tuned separately.

remember.title: Plug, unplug, restart — the route keeps up
remember.description: Device and process lists follow the audio engine on their own, no refresh button; routes remembered per program are restored the next time that program plays.

install.title: Three steps and you are routing
install.description: The installed build only needs Windows itself: no driver, no service.

one.title: Open the Releases page
one.description: Head to the GitHub Releases and find the newest release.

two.title: Download the installer
two.description: Grab the .msi installer, or the NSIS .exe setup.

three.title: Install and launch
three.description: Run it, launch App Audio Router, and play something in the program you want to route.

requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.webview: WebView2 runtime (bundled with Win11; present on any Win10 with Edge)
requirements.noDriver: No audio driver, no service, no third-party executable

build.title: Build from source
build.description: Needs Node.js 20+, pnpm 10 and a Rust toolchain with the MSVC target.
